evidence: Dimension weights: task/tests/scoring.toml:5-8 is functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, gates 0.0 (lines 1-3), functional floor 0.05 (line 11). It is byte-identical to the frozen template scoring.toml, and tests/tools/score.py is byte-identical to the template scorer (diff, no output). No weight key sits in any [judge] block. Maximum contribution of the non-functional dimensions is 0.40 and score.py:47-48 zeroes the reward unless functional > 0.05, so style cannot carry an app without working behaviour. Per-criterion weights, computed with tomllib: functional has 40 binary criteria, 13 at 1.0, 21 at 1.5 and 6 at 2.0, sum 56.5; polish has 6 binary criteria all 1.0; visual has 3 likert criteria all 1.0; gate criteria all 1.0. Inside functional the gradation tracks depth of proof: the six 2.0 criteria are the multi-step atomic or state-preserving behaviours (functional/judge.toml:99 cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic, :117 cw_same_line_carets, :189 cw_js_format_semantics_and_undo, :270 cw_last_good_recovery, :288 cw_stop_cancels_pending_work, :369 cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state); the 1.0 criteria are single-behaviour checks such as :27 cw_custom_typing_and_line_join, :180 cw_html_semantic_coloring, :252 cw_console_levels_in_order. Group mass: caret/selection/multi-caret/undo editing 16.0, find and replace 5.0, formatting 4.5, run/console/recovery 14.5, isolation and dynamic-code refusal 3.0, persistence/conflict/live update 11.0, syntax colouring 2.5. The only look-oriented functional criteria (colouring) hold 2.5/56.5 = 4.4 percent of functional, below every behaviour group, which matches a brief centred on a custom editor (overview.md:5, ui.md:3-17). I found no criterion whose weight exceeds what it proves and no structure-only criterion. The six polish criteria are behavioural (keyboard reach, focus return, unsaved marker, narrow-width use), so pure appearance is confined to the 0.2 visual dimension. Observation recorded, not a defect of this candidate: because the dimension split is template-fixed and functional needs 40 criteria for coverage, per-criterion reward mass is inverted. One functional criterion is worth 0.6*w/56.5 = 0.0106 (w 1.0), 0.0159 (w 1.5) or 0.0212 (w 2.0) of reward; one polish criterion is worth 0.2/6 = 0.0333; one visual likert criterion is worth 0.2/3 = 0.0667, about 0.0133 per likert step. So polish/judge.toml:45 cw_undo_redo_availability (disabled-state buttons, 0.0333) outweighs functional/judge.toml:321 cw_save_reload_restart (0.0159) and :270 cw_last_good_recovery (0.0212), and a single step of visual/judge.toml:119 cw_visual_component_finish outweighs functional/judge.toml:24 cw_custom_typing_and_line_join (0.0106). The visual dimension was also cut to 3 criteria against 6 in the template, which doubles each visual item's mass. In aggregate functionality still dominates (0.6 against 0.2 style), no weight is dishonest about what it proves, and the fix would need a change to shared scoring policy that AGENTS.md forbids, so the row is not failed. No runtime measurement is required for this row and none is claimed; no judge run, Oracle or model score was observed.
counterexample: Tried, not blocking. Weak app that could gain: App A loses the saved record on restart (fails cw_save_reload_restart, -0.0159) but disables Undo/Redo correctly (+0.0333); App B persists across restart but leaves Undo/Redo always enabled. A outscores B by 0.0174 on these two items alone, although the persistence gate cw_shared_saved_record still requires server-backed storage and both apps differ by one criterion each, so this is a per-item mass effect of the fixed 0.6/0.2/0.2 split and not a ranking inversion between a broadly worse and a broadly better app. Conforming alternative that could fail: none found for this row; weights do not reject any conforming implementation.
suggested_fix: Optional, no change required for clearance. If the owner wants per-item mass closer to proof value without touching scoring.toml or score.py: restore the visual dimension toward the template's six likert criteria (halving each item to 0.0333) and, if public requirements support it, split or add polish criteria so no single polish item exceeds the heaviest functional item. Do not change the template dimension weights or the floor.
